one_liner: Notion has a broad REST API with free self-serve tokens (internal connection, PAT) and OAuth 2.0 for public connections, plus an official hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 (token endpoint uses Basic client auth). Internal connection tokens and personal access tokens are static bearer tokens. Internal connections require workspace owner; pages must be shared with the connection.
access_notes: API available on all plans including Free; creating internal connections requires workspace owner, but anyone can create a free personal workspace. PAT creation is restricted by default on Business/Enterprise.
blocker_notes: No significant blocker; users must share pages with an internal connection or authorize via OAuth.

evidence.quote: personal access tokens use a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol
There’s no OAuth flow to implement — you get a token immediately when you create the connection, and you use that same token for every API request.
You can create an integration on any of the four plans, so your plan tier doesn't restrict your ability to build integrations
The Notion API accepts bearer tokens in this header.
Read, create, update, and search content; read and create comments; and read supported user information through Notion’s REST API.
Notion MCP is a remote MCP server hosted by Notion. After you authorize a connection with OAuth
